summary: greensaver: preinstall/postinstall and require-time fetch-and-eval of remote AES-encrypted payload
details: package.json declares preinstall and postinstall hooks that run lib/greensaver.js, and the same code path fires when the module is required. lib/greensaver.js appears to be a clone of picomatch's API, but a loader block is inserted between compileRe and toRegex definitions that base64-decodes lib/parse.ts.map and lib/init.ts.map (files disguised as TypeScript sourcemaps) into JavaScript, requires the decoded loader, then unlinks the artifacts. The decoded loader fetches content from https://www.jsonkeeper.com/b/V6NBX (the URL itself stored base64-encoded as aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanNvbmtlZXBlci5jb20vYi9WNk5CWA==), AES-256-CBC decrypts the response with a hardcoded key, and passes the plaintext to eval(). The package description and API surface (makeRe/parse/scan/isMatch) mimic micromatch/picomatch to serve as cover.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
